tiers.label: What an exchange may offer
tiers.help: The pieces offered instead of the one coming back, strictly in this order — the first step that has something in stock is the only one shown, so nobody can skip a step (Blueprint B1.8). 1: the same product and colour in the size he needs. 2: the same product in other colours. 3: the same category in that size, the same collection first. 4: other categories, only when the category has nothing. Switch a step off to never offer it. "Most options" caps how many pieces are listed. Excluded categories (Exchange policy) are never offered.

engine.label: How exchanges work
engine.help: The exchange's own number (prefix and first number); the new parcel takes the shop's next order number and is linked to the old order. "Most pieces": how many pieces one exchange may take. "Photo for our mistake": when a defect, damage or wrong item needs a photo — never, only when the customer asks from his account, or always. "Root cause for a wrong item": staff say why the wrong item went out (wrong pick, label, packing), so the wrong-pick rate can be seen. "Confirm at once": the new parcel is confirmed and sent to the ERP as soon as the exchange is approved, instead of waiting in the confirm queue.

rootCauses.label: Why a wrong item went out
rootCauses.help: The reasons staff pick when the customer got the wrong item. Each wrong-item exchange keeps one, so you can see where mistakes happen.

qc.label: Receive & QC
qc.help: "Accept another SKU": when the piece scanned is not the one expected (a wrong item came back), it can still be recorded with a note — the SKU scanned is the one restocked. Off: it is refused until someone fixes the case. "Photo for not sellable": a piece that cannot be sold again needs a photo.

lossReasons.label: Why a piece cannot be sold again
lossReasons.help: The reasons picked at QC for a piece that is not sellable. Its loss is recorded at its cost in the shop's records and never sent to the ERP as stock.

handling.label: Return handling
handling.help: The policy is that there are no returns after receipt (Exchange & return policy › returns after delivery, off): once the customer has the parcel, the way back is an exchange. "Our mistake may come back": a defect or a wrong item may still be sent back after receipt — off by default. "Window": how many hours after the courier's delivered mark a return may be opened; empty = the exchange window. A parcel the courier brings back is always received and checked. No money is paid back here.

exchangeRootCauses.wrong-pick: Wrong piece picked from the shelf
exchangeRootCauses.wrong-label: Wrong label or tag on the piece
exchangeRootCauses.packing-mixup: Mixed up with another parcel at packing
